questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

This artwork / are a wonderful example / of the period's vogue / for realistic style.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the incorrect use of the verb "**are**" which should be "**is**" to agree with the singular subject "**artwork**."
 
• Singular subjects require singular verbs, while plural subjects require plural verbs.
 
• The correct phrase should be "**is a wonderful example**," ensuring grammatical correctness and clarity.
 
• Thus, the error is located in **Option 3** of the sentence.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"This artwork **is a wonderful example** of the period's vogue for realistic style."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "of the period's vogue,"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **Option 2: "for realistic style,"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **Option 4: "This artwork,"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.

questions.question:

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the incorrect use of the preposition "**in**" in the phrase "**giving in the prizes**."
 
• The correct preposition to use with the verb "**give**" in this context is "**away**."
 
• The correct phrase should be "**giving away the prizes**," ensuring grammatical correctness and clarity.
 
• Thus, the error is located in **Option 4** of the sentence.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The companies were **giving away__ the prizes** to attract customers during the festive season."*

• **Option 3: "The companies were,"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.

questions.question:
Identify the error in the following sentence and select the option with the correct use of the phrasal verb.

Prateek was planning to ask Shreya for a favour. But he could not muster up the courage. So, he blacked out.

options.text: Prateek was planning to ask Shreya for a favour. But he could not muster up the courage. So, he turned down.
Prateek was planning to ask Shreya for a favour. But he could not muster up the courage. So, he checked out.
Prateek was planning to ask Shreya for a favour. But he could not muster up the courage. So, he chickened out.
Prateek was planning to ask Shreya for a favour. But he could not muster up the courage. So, he broke in.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the incorrect use of the phrasal verb **"blacked out."**
 
• **"Blacked out"** means to lose consciousness, which does not fit the context of the sentence.
 
• The correct phrasal verb should be **"chickened out,**" which means to lose courage or decide not to do something out of fear.
 
• Thus, the error is located in the last part of the sentence.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Prateek was planning to ask Shreya for a favour. But he could not muster up the courage. So, he **chickened out**."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "turned down"** – This means to reject something, which does not fit the context.
 
• **Option 2: "checked out"** – This means to leave or depart, which does not fit the context.
 
• **Option 4: "broke in"** – This means to enter by force, which does not fit the context.

questions.question: The balloon started to deflate after being pricked with a needle. What is the ANTONYM of ‘deflate’?
